title: Every container gets its own thin writable layer
subtitle: The image underneath is read-only and shared. Changes go into the container's own layer, and die with it.

nodes.label: writable layer of layers-a

24.6kB

areas.label: Image layers-cow: read-only
areas.detail: shared by both containers, never changed by them

notes.text:
Copy-on-write: to change a file that came from the image, Docker first copies it up into the container's layer, then changes the copy. The image's file stays as it was.

docker rm throws the writable layer away. The image is untouched, so the next container starts fresh.

docker diff layers-a
# A = added, C = changed, D = deleted
docker ps -as
